title: Range Stops Before Limit
objective: Understand that range(3) generates numbers 0, 1, 2 excluding 3

scenes.heading: Range Stops Before Limit
scenes.narration: The range function creates a sequence starting from zero up to a specific limit number. Crucially, the upper number provided is never included in the final sequence. So range(3) yields exactly 0, 1, and 2, stopping just before it reaches 3.

scenes.heading: Concrete Example Walkthrough
scenes.narration: The code starts by defining a loop that visits every item in the 0, 1, 2 sequence. The variable i takes each number in turn as the program executes the body line by line. Finally, print(i) outputs 0, then 1, then 2 on separate lines, confirming the upper limit is excluded.

scenes.heading: Common Mistake Alert
scenes.narration: Students often mistakenly believe range(3) starts at 1 or includes 3 in the count. The correct sequence supplies a value to print that stops strictly before 3. The upper limit is excluded, so the loop has three iterations.

followUp: Practice writing loops with different limit values to reinforce the exclusion rule.
